heroHeadline: Warsh Signals $6.7T Balance Sheet Reduction — 'Blow Up the Playbook'; USTR Greer: US Can Restore China Tariffs to 'Busan Deal' ~41.6%; Section 122 CIT Ruling Under Federal Circuit Stay; Goldman 30%, Moody's 49% Recession Risk
heroSubtitle: On Day 3 of Kevin Warsh's Federal Reserve chairmanship (May 17, 2026), multiple analyses revealed that the new Fed Chair intends to aggressively reduce the $6.7 trillion Federal Reserve balance sheet — which stood at only $900 billion before the 2008 financial crisis. Warsh argues the balance sheet 'disproportionately helps those with financial assets' and wants to 'blow up the playbook that has kept stocks rising for 15 years.' Analysts warn this could push the US 10-year Treasury yield above its current 4.59% weekly close (already the highest since May 2025) toward 5.00%+ — compressing the Shiller CAPE ratio of ~38.6 and tightening financial conditions even before any rate hike. Separately, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer appeared on CBS Face the Nation to signal that the post-Trump-Xi summit trade architecture now includes formalized US-China Trade and Investment Boards — the first such mechanisms in history — while explicitly warning that the US can restore China tariffs to the 'Busan Deal' level (~41.6%, up from the current ~31.6%) if diplomatic momentum stalls. On the legal front, the US Court of International Trade ruled (May 7, 2-1) that Section 122 tariffs were unlawful — but the Federal Circuit issued an administrative stay on May 12, keeping tariffs active through the appeal process. The Section 122 cliff of July 23 (66 days) remains the primary policy deadline. Recession probabilities are unchanged at Goldman 30%, JPMorgan 35%, and Moody's 49%; Bank of America continues to forecast no Fed cuts until July 2027. The week ahead includes April housing starts (May 21) and Flash PMIs (May 22) — the first post-summit reads on the real economy.
footerNote: Data sourced from Motley Fool (Warsh $6.7T balance sheet, May 17 2026), CBS News Face the Nation transcript (USTR Greer, May 17 2026), Gibson Dunn / Thompson Coburn / BDO (CIT Section 122 ruling, May 7 2026), Share Talk Weekly (FTSE 100 -1.9%, May 17 2026), TheStreet (Goldman Sachs 30% / BofA no-cut warning, May 16 2026), JPMorgan Mid-Year Outlook 2026, Moody's Analytics, Federal Reserve H.15 / FRED DGS10 (10Y yield 4.59%), BLS April 2026 CPI/PPI, BEA Q1 2026 GDP, US Census Bureau April Retail Sales.
